analysis:
Changed lines: ProviderLoop+Serve.swift:108 sets `verifiedWeightHashesFile = VerifiedWeightHashStore.path()` when `usesHostServices` is true. ProviderLoop+Testing.swift adds two test seams (setVerifiedWeightHashesFileForTesting, setLoadWeightHasherForTesting), which lie outside any #if DEBUG block in the visible base text. They are internal, not public, and are used via @testable import. They let a caller redirect the verified-hash file or replace the hasher, but only an in-process caller could use them, which already implies code execution in the provider. That is consistent with the existing T-013/T-014 assumptions, so I treat this as no new attack surface. The production path leaves the hasher default untouched, and the test seam is not wired into production flows in the supplied evidence.

The new verified-hash store appears to persist managed-load weight hashes to a file. This relates to T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution). I could not see VerifiedWeightHashStore.path(), its file permissions, whether it is owner-only, how it is read back, or whether a stored hash is trusted without re-verification. A tampered file could weaken weight-hash assurance if later consumers treat it as authoritative. Other changes to loadWeightHasher, captureWeightHash and the consumers of verifiedWeightHashesFile are not in this batch. The hash store is a local-operator-controlled file, and the operator is already adversarial under T-012, so the store must not be a trust root. This is a question for integration, not a finding. No cache-storage (T-041), attestation, or coordinator-wire behavior changed in these units. Remaining questions: VerifiedWeightHashStore file location, permissions and no-follow handling, whether the stored hashes are reported to the coordinator as attested evidence, and whether the file is bound to the model revision.
